## Introduction

In this post, I explore the Palmer Penguins dataset using Python. I examine differences in body mass and flipper length among penguin species and visualize the relationship between these measurements.

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/), Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

## Loading and exploring the data

First, I load the Palmer Penguins dataset and examine its structure.

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins.head()
```
## Missing values

Before analyzing the measurements, I check how many missing values occur in each variable.

```{python}
penguins.isna().sum()
```
## Summary by species

Next, I calculate the average body mass and flipper length for each penguin species.

```{python}
species_summary = (
    penguins
    .groupby("species")
    .agg(
        average_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        average_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean")
    )
    .round(2)
)

species_summary
```
## Relationship between body mass and flipper length

Finally, I visualize the relationship between body mass and flipper length for each penguin species.

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-measurements
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between body mass and flipper length across penguin species."

for species, group in penguins.groupby("species"):
    plt.scatter(
        group["flipper_length_mm"],
        group["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7
    )

plt.xlabel("Flipper Length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)")
plt.title("Body Mass vs. Flipper Length")
plt.legend(title="Species")
plt.show()
```

The plot suggests a positive relationship between flipper length and body mass. Penguins with longer flippers generally have greater body mass, while the species also form distinct groups.
